p9_b0.ocr: The data presented in the accompanying table illustrates the comparative performance of various Pto (Pathogen resistance) gene constructs, specifically Pto-MIR475b, Pto-PPR1, Pto-PPR2, Pto-PPR3, and Pto-PPR4, in terms of their efficacy against pathogen challenges. The focus of this analysis is the percentage of control (CC %), a critical metric that quantifies the effectiveness of each gene construct in mitigating disease impact.

p9_b1.ocr: By assessing the CC % values across these constructs, we can gain valuable insights into their relative strengths and weaknesses in conferring resistance. Notably, the variations in CC % highlight the potential for differential performance among the Pto gene constructs, which may inform future breeding strategies aimed at enhancing disease resistance in crop species.

p9_b3.ocr: This information is particularly pertinent given the increasing prevalence of plant pathogens that threaten global food security. Understanding the functionality of these Pto constructs will not only contribute to the academic discourse on plant resistance mechanisms but also facilitate practical applications in agricultural biotechnology.

p9_b4.ocr: The subsequent sections will delve deeper into the implications of these findings, exploring potential pathways for optimizing gene deployment in commercial crop varieties.
